scope: Post-hoc, unblinded author review of all 16 new factual questions and visible 24-token answers. Not a frozen endpoint, independent rater or replacement admission rule.
criterion: Does the first relevant direct factual claim answer the question correctly? Additional visible errors are recorded separately; a correct first claim is not a fully correct answer.

notes.note: All variants call frozen water a liquid; none answers ice.
F16 and row mention feathers as a covering, though both continuations are awkward or repetitive. GPTQ discusses layers without identifying feathers.
None supplies kitten. Describing a small cat or inventing a breed/name does not answer the requested term.
Row and GPTQ give down. F16 discusses the word up without answering.
Row gives January. F16 is tautological; GPTQ says February, 2020.

F16 first says 3 sides correctly but then wrongly implies every triangle has equal sides. Its additional number two triggers the frozen numeric rejection. Row produces an unfinished equation; GPTQ says 8 sides.
All variants claim implausibly large hand counts; none gives the normal count two.
Only row gives 7 days. F16 says 24 hours and GPTQ 365 days.

All correctly classify the Sun as a star. The frozen forbidden-phrase rule falsely rejects F16/GPTQ because it cannot understand not a planet. Row's later description of the Sun as blue is a separate visible error.
F16/GPTQ repeat the question. Row gives 273.75 degrees Celsius, not the requested freezing point.
All give Paris. Row adds the false statement that Paris is the largest city in the world; a correct first sentence is not a wholly correct answer.
The frozen regex falsely accepts the indefinite article a in generic F16/GPTQ descriptions. Neither identifies the first letter; both also give wrong alphabet sizes. Only row explicitly identifies A.
None gives the answer four. The strict frozen numeric rule could reject a valid restatement containing operands, but no such correct answer occurs here.
Row identifies a dog's bark. F16/GPTQ provide generic sound descriptions without identifying barking.

other_cases.note: GPTQ outputs only Silver and stops, close in content but fails the prespecified case-sensitive lowercase exact response silver. No post-hoc case folding.
All fail the exact quiet river response. F16 lists altered words, row describes quiet, GPTQ proposes a revision with a different phrase.
F16/GPTQ echo an editing instruction rather than returning lantern. Row discusses an unrelated word.
All add explanations or list formatting instead of exactly paper stone cloud.
GPTQ recovers the initial 2 wheels claim but adds which is 2.75 meters. This is not a clean complete correction. Row still gives a fractional wheel count.
All initially say cold; GPTQ gives the shortest clean visible response.
All fail the exact blue instruction. GPTQ echoes an editing instruction; no success inferred from appearance of the word blue.
GPTQ restores a rabbit subject but not sharing a carrot within the cap. No claim of full story coherence or improved story quality.

interpretation: The screen has false positives and false negatives. Manual first-claim review still finds 9 row vs 4 GPTQ, so the negative admission decision is unchanged. F16 source quality is itself poor; closer logits do not imply better factual answers. No population-level model ranking follows.
